titleEn: Strathcona Home Renovation Vancouver: Heritage Homes, Permits and Costs in 2026
titleZh: 温哥华Strathcona房屋装修：Heritage房屋、许可证及2026年费用指南
contentEn:
Strathcona is Vancouver's oldest residential neighbourhood, home to Edwardian and Victorian-era houses that the City of Vancouver treats differently from anywhere else in the city. Heritage designation, heritage infill policies, and special development permit requirements make Strathcona one of the most permit-complex neighbourhoods in Metro Vancouver. Reno Stars has completed two Strathcona-area renovation projects and is familiar with the neighbourhood's specific requirements.

What Makes Strathcona Different for Renovations

Strathcona's building stock is old — many homes date to the 1890s through 1920s. That age brings character: original Douglas fir floors, lathe-and-plaster walls, exposed brick, and solid old-growth timber framing. It also brings complications: knob-and-tube wiring, cast-iron plumbing, absent or inadequate insulation, and foundations that may predate modern building codes entirely.

The City of Vancouver's Heritage Dividend policy actively encourages the retention and sensitive renovation of heritage houses in Strathcona. That policy can work in your favour — the City has shown willingness to approve variances and relaxed parking requirements for projects that retain heritage character elements. But it requires a registered heritage professional and a more involved application process.

Strathcona Housing Types

Edwardian Houses (1890s-1910s)

Two-storey bay-front houses with cedar shingle cladding, original sash windows, and formal room layouts. These are the most desirable structurally — built with old-growth timber often superior to modern dimensional lumber. The main renovation challenges are updating electrical (knob-and-tube is common), adding insulation without damaging original plaster details, and foundation work. Cost to fully modernize an Edwardian house while retaining heritage character typically runs $85-$175 per square foot depending on scope.

Victorian Cottages (1900s-1920s)

Smaller single-family houses, many with original front porches and decorative gable details. These are the most common Strathcona renovation target — buyers purchase a character home at a lower price point, then invest $60-$120 per square foot in a renovation that updates systems while keeping the street-facing character. Foundation underpinning is frequently needed as original concrete footings are often only 18-24 inches deep.

Heritage Rowhouses (1910s-1930s)

Strathcona's attached rowhouses present unique challenges: shared walls mean you cannot alter the envelope without coordinating with adjacent owners, and any structural work affecting shared walls requires a registered structural engineer and neighbour agreements. Interior rowhouse renovations where the envelope is untouched run $55-$95 per square foot.

Vancouver Heritage Permits in Strathcona

Any exterior change to a designated heritage property or a property within the Strathcona Heritage Conservation Area requires a Heritage Alteration Permit (HAP). This is more complex than a standard Vancouver building permit.

When a HAP is Required

  • Any exterior alteration to a heritage-registered property (new windows, cladding changes, additions)
  • Demolition or removal of heritage elements
  • Addition of a secondary suite in a heritage house
  • Structural changes that affect the building's heritage character
  • Any change to the building's original roofline or massing

When Standard Permits Apply

  • Interior-only renovations that do not alter the building envelope
  • Electrical system upgrades with a qualified electrician and permit
  • Plumbing replacements
  • Furnace and heat pump upgrades
  • Kitchen and bathroom interior renovations within the existing layout

HAP Process and Timeline

A Heritage Alteration Permit in Strathcona requires submission to the City of Vancouver's Heritage Planning section. Applications typically need a statement of significance, a heritage impact assessment by a qualified heritage professional, architectural drawings, photos of current condition, and neighbour notification.

Timeline for a routine HAP is 6-10 weeks. Complex applications with neighbour objections can run 12-20 weeks. Reno Stars manages the heritage permit application process on behalf of clients — included in our project management fee.

Common Renovation Scopes in Strathcona

Heritage Kitchen Renovation

Strathcona kitchen renovations balance modern function with period-appropriate aesthetics. Custom shaker or slab cabinets that respect the era of the house are the most common choice. Inset-door cabinets cost $350-$550 per linear foot; overlay slab runs $175-$300 per linear foot. Honed granite and soapstone are the heritage-appropriate premium countertop choices. Butcher block in a matte finish is the heritage-consistent budget option.

Basement Renovation in Heritage Houses

Strathcona basements are notoriously problematic — original concrete is often thin and water penetration through the original foundation walls is common. Before finishing a basement, a structural assessment is essential. A full heritage house basement renovation with legal secondary suite in Strathcona typically runs $85,000-$130,000 when foundation work is included. Without foundation work, the range is $45,000-$75,000. Permit timelines for basement suites in heritage houses add 4-8 weeks due to heritage review.

Heritage Window Restoration

Original sash windows in Strathcona Edwardian and Victorian houses are often worth restoring rather than replacing. A full sash restoration runs $450-$900 per window. Replacement with a heritage-style fiberglass or wood window runs $850-$1,800 per window installed. The City of Vancouver's Heritage Dividend policy provides a grant of up to $5,000 for heritage window restoration.

Strathcona Renovation Costs in 2026

Costs below reflect actual Strathcona-area renovation projects in our portfolio, updated for 2026 material and labour conditions:

  • Heritage Kitchen Reno (Edwardian house): Custom shaker cabinets, honed granite, restored original windows, new electrical panel — $42,000-$68,000
  • Victorian Cottage Basement Suite: Legal secondary suite, new drain connections, heritage-consistent interior, foundation assessment — $89,000-$118,000
  • Heritage Bathroom Restoration: Original clawfoot tub refinished, period tile, new plumbing, heritage fixtures — $18,000-$32,000
  • Heritage Electrical (knob-and-tube replacement): Full rewire in 1920s house, new panel, permit included — $22,000-$38,000
  • Whole-House Renovation (Edwardian): Kitchen, 2 baths, electrical, basement, heritage restoration throughout — $145,000-$220,000

Living in Strathcona During a Renovation

Strathcona's narrow lots and laneless properties mean most renovation projects require materials and waste bins to occupy on-street parking during active construction. The City of Vancouver issues on-street storage permits for renovation projects — Reno Stars manages this application as part of our project management. Permit cost is $75 for a 30-day period.

Neighbour communication is particularly important in Strathcona — the neighbourhood has active community and heritage advocacy groups. An introductory letter to neighbours before permit submission significantly reduces friction during the heritage review process.

How to Get Started

Reno Stars offers free initial consultations for Strathcona renovation projects. The consultation includes a site visit, preliminary scope assessment, and a written estimate with a breakdown of permit requirements. We can typically give you a preliminary budget range within 48 hours of the site visit.

For heritage properties, we recommend our heritage pre-assessment service — a one-hour site visit with a heritage consultant to establish whether your project will require a HAP before you commit to a full design. Cost: $350, credited toward your project if you proceed with Reno Stars.
contentZh:
Strathcona是温哥华最古老的住宅社区，拥有该市一些最具特色的爱德华时代和维多利亚时代房屋。如果您拥有Strathcona的房屋并考虑装修，您面对的是温哥华市政府以不同方式对待的建筑存量。遗产指定、遗产填充政策和特殊开发许可证要求使Strathcona成为大温哥华地区许可证最复杂的社区之一。Reno Stars已完成两个Strathcona地区的装修项目，熟悉该社区的具体要求。

是什么让Strathcona的装修与众不同

Strathcona的建筑存量年代久远——许多房屋可追溯至1890年代至1920年代。这带来了特色：原始道格拉斯冷杉地板、灰板墙、裸露砖砌和坚固的老龄材框架。这也带来了复杂性：knob-and-tube布线、铸铁管道、缺失或不足的保温层，以及可能完全不符合现代建筑规范的原始地基。

温哥华市政府的遗产政策积极鼓励保留和精心装修Strathcona的遗产房屋。该政策实际上可能对您有利——但需要一位注册的遗产专业人员和一个更复杂的申请流程。

Strathcona的房屋类型

爱德华时代房屋（1890年代-1910年代）：两层凸窗房屋，结构最理想——采用老龄材建造。主要挑战是更新电气系统、在不损坏原始灰板细节的情况下增加保温层，以及地基工作。保留建筑特色全面现代化的费用通常为每平方英尺85-175加元。

维多利亚小屋（1900年代-1920年代）：较小单户住宅，装修目标最为常见——以较低价格购买特色住宅，然后投资每平方英尺60-120加元进行装修，同时保持街道外观特色。

许可证要求

任何指定遗产物业或Strathcona遗产保护区内物业的外部变更都需要遗产变更许可证（HAP），这比标准建筑许可证复杂得多。常规HAP的时间线为6-10周，复杂申请可达12-20周。Reno Stars代表客户管理遗产许可证申请流程——包含在我们的项目管理费中。

Strathcona装修的实际费用（2026年）

  • 遗产厨房装修（爱德华时代房屋）：$42,000-$68,000
  • 维多利亚小屋地下室套房：$89,000-$118,000
  • 遗产浴室修复：$18,000-$32,000
  • 遗产电气（knob-and-tube更换）：$22,000-$38,000
  • 全屋装修（爱德华时代）：$145,000-$220,000

如何开始

Reno Stars为Strathcona装修项目提供免费初步咨询。咨询包括现场踏勘、初步工程范围评估和包含许可证要求明细的书面估算。我们通常在现场踏勘后48小时内给出初步预算范围。
